title: GE Vernova — Data Access Portal
oneLiner: Django backend for a financial visualization platform with natural-language query workflows and automated report migration.
problem: Analysts needed a faster way to generate structured JSON templates and query cloud datasets, while a large report migration had to happen with minimal manual work.
solution: Built Django REST APIs, SQL-to-JSON translation and validation pipelines, and automated migration scripts for templates and reports.
architecture: Python/Django REST API over SQL-backed cloud datasets, with validation between natural-language-driven query intent and generated JSON structures.

decisions.question: Why automate the migration?
decisions.answer: The migration involved 130+ blank templates and 10,000 associated reports, making scripted transfer more reliable and repeatable than manual movement.

lessons: Query translation is only useful when paired with validation; correctness and predictable output matter as much as generation speed.

title: GE Vernova — Data Archival Portal
oneLiner: Low-cost enterprise archival and search platform using S3 cold storage, Athena row-level security, and OpenSearch.
problem: Enterprise project metadata and files needed cheaper long-term storage while remaining searchable and securely exportable.
solution: Architected an S3-based archival workflow, implemented row-level security over Athena queries, and added paginated OpenSearch APIs for full-text retrieval.
architecture: Django REST APIs coordinate archival metadata and secure query workflows across S3, Athena and OpenSearch, with pagination to keep large result sets predictable.

decisions.question: Why combine S3, Athena and OpenSearch?
decisions.answer: The system needed inexpensive durable storage, SQL-style secure access to structured data, and low-friction full-text search for encrypted files.

lessons: Storage, query and search concerns can be separated into fit-for-purpose services while the API layer provides a stable interface to clients.

title: GE Vernova — Vernova Data Portal
oneLiner: Backend revamp of a legacy enterprise portal around hierarchical domain-based access and embedded analytics.
problem: The legacy portal needed a clearer access model and a modern backend foundation for embedded analytics and chatbot experiences.
solution: Led the backend revamp, established hierarchical domain-based access, and integrated Tableau/Spotfire reports and a custom chatbot through iframes.
architecture: Python/Django REST APIs provide the access-control and application layer while embedded analytics surfaces remain integrated into the portal UI.
lessons: A backend modernization is often as much about defining a clean access model as replacing implementation details.

title: Job Market Intelligence
oneLiner: Scheduled Django data pipeline for collecting and structuring job-market intelligence.
problem: Job-market research becomes difficult to compare when opportunities, requirements and market signals are collected manually and inconsistently.
solution: A Django-based scheduled collection pipeline with a defined data schema and repeatable ingestion workflow.
architecture: Django application with scheduled data collection and structured persistence. Detailed ingestion and storage decisions will be documented as the build progresses.
lessons: The project is intentionally being kept narrow until the core data pipeline is reliable.

title: Job Apply Bot
oneLiner: Automated job-application workflow using scheduled GitHub Actions, tiered risk scoring, and Claude-powered resume tailoring.
problem: Manual applications are slow and inconsistent when every role requires a separate evaluation and resume-tailoring step.
solution: GitHub Actions scheduling triggers a tiered risk-scoring workflow; matched roles can receive Claude-tailored resume output before the application step.
architecture: Scheduled automation → role evaluation → risk tier → tailored resume generation, with the workflow designed to separate low-risk automation from decisions that need review.

decisions.question: Why a tiered risk model?
decisions.answer: Not every automated application action has the same downside, so the workflow separates lower-risk automation from higher-risk actions that should be reviewed.

lessons: Automation should encode risk boundaries instead of treating every action as equally safe to execute unattended.

title: The Paradigm
oneLiner: Django + Next.js infrastructure for a technical publishing platform with structured content and an eventual grounded assistant.
problem: Technical writing needs a content system that can grow beyond a collection of static pages without coupling the publishing model to the presentation layer.
solution: Django provides the backend/content model while Next.js handles the public experience, keeping the architecture ready for richer knowledge features later.
architecture: Django backend + Next.js frontend, with the content model separated from presentation and a future retrieval-grounded assistant planned around the stored knowledge.
lessons: Build the content foundation before adding intelligence features; a grounded assistant needs real, structured material to retrieve.

title: This Portfolio
oneLiner: Static Next.js portfolio backed by Django for dynamic contact handling, designed as an evidence-linked engineering document.
problem: A resume lists technologies but rarely shows the reasoning, constraints, or measurable outcomes behind them.
solution: Static-export Next.js serves read-heavy portfolio content cheaply and quickly; Django is reserved for dynamic backend behavior such as contact handling and the future grounded assistant.
architecture: JSON content → static Next.js pages → CDN-friendly output, with a separate Django API for dynamic behavior. Docker provides a repeatable local backend environment.

decisions.question: Why static + Django API?
decisions.answer: Most portfolio content does not change per request, so static delivery is a better fit; Django remains only where server-side behavior adds value.

decisions.question: Why evidence links?
decisions.answer: The portfolio should make technical claims inspectable instead of asking a recruiter or interviewer to take them on faith.

lessons: Content quality comes before the AI assistant: retrieval is only useful when there is real engineering material to ground it on.
